title: Buy Now Pay Later Scam
summary: Video compiles clips arguing BNPL creates untracked 'phantom debt' that could mirror risks seen before the 2008 financial crisis.

assertions.quote: BNPL businesses aren't under the same reporting obligations as banks or credit agencies

verdicts.note: Directionally true that reporting gaps limit visibility, but Federal Reserve and CFPB surveys do capture meaningful aggregate data, so 'cannot measure' overstates the gap.

assertions.quote: 63% of BNPL borrowers had simultaneous loans at some point
financial institutions knowingly giving out home loans their clients couldn't pay back

verdicts.note: Some structural parallels exist (easy credit, growth outpacing oversight), but BNPL's dollar scale and securitization footprint are far smaller than 2008-era subprime mortgages, so a full repeat is unlikely.

assertions.quote: Deep subprime consumers alone make up 45% of BNPL loans, with another 16% coming from subprime borrowers.
Average BNPL users have 4% more overdraft charges

verdicts.note: Confirmed mechanistically and by Federal Reserve survey data showing a meaningful share of users reporting BNPL-triggered overdraft or NSF fees.
KC Fed: even with auto-repayments set up, a nominally interest-free BNPL installment can still trigger an overdraft or NSF fee if the linked account lacks sufficient funds.
